qs.q: A patient with an apical lung mass, Horner syndrome, and ulnar nerve pain. What is the diagnosis?
o: Pancoast (superior sulcus) tumour at the lung apex.
Superior vena cava obstruction causing facial swelling.
qs.e: Pancoast tumors occur at the lung apex and invade the sympathetic chain (Horner syndrome) and the brachial plexus (C8-T2 distribution pain).
